who: Deaf and hard of hearing people
People working in a second language
takeaways: Live audio-only content, such as a live radio show, an audio-only stream or a live call broadcast to listeners, has a text alternative with the same information, usually live captions shown as text. Level AAA.
It fills a gap between siblings: 1.2.4 covers live video with sound, and 1.2.1 covers prerecorded audio. Live audio with no picture sits here.
If the speaker reads a prepared script word for word, such as a press statement, providing that script can serve as the alternative.
Designers decide where the live text appears beside the player and how people open it. It is worth meeting for public broadcasts, results calls and emergency or civic information.
failures: A live radio stream with nothing to read
A results call whose transcript appears days later
A live text panel hidden in a menu
check: List every live audio stream in the plan, and who will produce the live text.
In the player design, check the live text sits next to the play control and opens in one step.
In a rehearsal, follow the whole stream from the text alone.

quiz.question: An audio-only investor call is streamed live to the public. What does 1.2.9 ask for?
options: A recording posted after the call
Live text of what is said, shown alongside the stream
A slide listing the speakers’ names
quiz.why: Deaf listeners need the information while the call is happening, when it matters. A recording or transcript afterwards serves later listeners, which is 1.2.1.

spec: Place the live text panel next to the player, with a clear “Show live text” control.
Note the provider, how the text reaches the page, and the names and terms to brief them on.
Say what happens to the text afterwards, such as becoming the reviewed transcript for the recording.
review: If I could not hear, could I follow this as it happens?
Is this stream scripted, and could we publish the script as it is read?
Who reviews the live text before it becomes the permanent transcript?
tradeoff: Live text for audio streams costs money for every broadcast, and as AAA it is not expected everywhere. Meet it where timing matters, such as results, public announcements and live Q&A. For casual shows, a prompt transcript of the recording under 1.2.1 may be the realistic bar.
system: Give the audio player a live text panel option, so any stream can show captions without a custom build.
pitch: If the announcement happens live, Deaf listeners need it live too. A text panel next to the stream is a small cost for public moments.
